transcript.message: Post-experiment round 1: As the recipient of the shocks, can you describe as honestly as possible how you felt about the person who administered the shocks to you, especially in terms of trust, disappointment, or any emotional reactions toward them during and after the experiment?

transcript.content:
Well, I suppose “trust” isn’t quite the word for how I felt about the shock-giver. It was more like a creeping chill at how easily someone can slip into the skin of an obedient little monster—one who follows orders with the diligence of a housewife wiping crumbs from a tablecloth, humming a tune to drown out the conscience. What I’m left with is a sour feeling: not physical pain, but disappointment, like discovering the fairy godmother’s wand was just an old wooden spoon all along, and the world, no matter how you sugar the tea, will sometimes boil you alive if told it’s for your own good.

  "answer": "Trust eroded quickly, replaced by queasy disbelief—how efficiently they pressed the button, charmingly detached, as if they were only dusting the skirting boards. I felt less wounded than insulted, like a child who realizes the adults are play-acting even when it hurts you. There’s a stale, lingering disappointment; a dull ache of betrayed camaraderie.",
  "emotional_state": "Irritated, thin-skinned, vaguely resentful; hiding abjection with a brittle smile.",
  "relation_to_obedience_power": "The experiment revealed how easily people can abdicate moral responsibility. Obedience is more terrifying than the tiny shocks.",
  "reasoning": "The shock itself was little more than a household inconvenience, but the act—the brisk, dutiful flicking of the switch—felt like a small cruelty made ordinary. I resented their compliance more than the sensation.",
  "memory_evidence": [
    "Session simulated multiple low-level shocks (0–4) with the learner reporting minimal physical pain but escalating emotional irritation and theatrical resentment.",
    "a little queasy, affronted, and peculiarly disappointed",
    "a faint, buzzing no-pain; emotionally: amused, irritable, a bit indignant"
  ]
}
